prompt: Implement allocator_trace(free_extents, header, events), a deterministic first-fit allocator over abstract integer byte positions. This is a fixed-region model of layout, splitting and adjacent coalescing, not malloc, physical RAM, or a typed-object lifetime simulator. Position 0 is a valid model address; failure is represented by None. free_extents is a list of 0–8 two-element lists [begin,end] with native integer positions 0<=begin<end<=4096. Extents are disjoint but may be adjacent or supplied out of order. Initially sort and transitively coalesce all adjacent extents. Unlisted positions are unavailable throughout. header is an int from 0 to 16; all integers in this task exclude bool. events contains at most 64 exact records: {op:'alloc',id:str,size:int,align:int} or {op:'free',id:str}. IDs are case-sensitive ASCII strings matching [A-Za-z0-9_]{1,12}; every alloc ID is globally fresh, including failed requests. size is 1–128; align is a power of two from 1 to 128. Every free names a currently live successful allocation. For alloc, examine current free extents in increasing begin order and select the first that fits: for extent [b,e), payload start p is the smallest multiple of align >=b+header; fit requires p+size<=e. Use exact integer arithmetic. Only the payload has an alignment requirement; header bytes and leading padding consume the prefix before p. On success consume the whole prefix [b,p+size), record live[id]={extent:[b,p+size],payload:p,size:size}, retain any positive remainder [p+size,e), and report allocated with address=p. There is no minimum split size, trailing rounding, growth, relocation, or fallback. On failure report failed with address=None and change neither free nor live state. On free, remove that live record, return its ENTIRE stored extent including header/padding to the free set, sort and transitively coalesce adjacent extents, and report freed with address=None. Return a list of independent snapshots AFTER each event, or [] for no events. Each snapshot has exactly {op,id,status,address,free,live}; free is the sorted maximally coalesced interval list, and live maps current IDs to the exact three-field records above. Dict key order does not matter; interval order does. All containers and scalars are exact built-in dict/list/str/int/None values. Do not mutate inputs, including during a later call. Every snapshot and every call must have independent mutable output containers; do not reuse cached shared results or retain cross-call state. Inputs satisfy these schemas/preconditions; no outside-domain validation is required. Use only the standard library, without actual memory allocation APIs, threads or network.

Implement trace_collection(graph, roots, young=None), a pure analyzer of a declared complete, fixed strong-reference graph. graph is an exact built-in dict with 0–16 object IDs as keys and exact built-in lists of 0–32 target IDs as values, at most 256 edges total. Every target is an existing key. IDs are case-sensitive ASCII matching [A-Za-z0-9_]{1,12}. roots is an exact built-in list of 0–32 existing IDs. Repeated roots and edges do not create duplicate discoveries. young is None by default, or an exact built-in list of distinct existing IDs, possibly empty. The complete graph and root snapshot has no mutations, hidden roots, weak edges, finalizers, pins, or special liveness rules. With young=None, select all graph objects, set incoming to empty, mark the least strong-edge closure of roots, and classify all remaining objects as unmarked. With young a list, select exactly its set Y. Derive incoming as the set of ALL targets in Y of edges whose source lies outside Y, regardless of whether that outside source is globally reachable or a direct root. This complete input-derived incoming set models complete remembered information; computing it here is not a claim about a real young collector's scan cost. Seed marked with roots in Y plus incoming, then close only over edges whose target remains inside Y. Objects outside Y never appear in marked or unmarked. Because the uncollected outside population is conservatively treated as potential liveness sources, an unreachable old object can retain its young target; full collection of the same graph can classify both objects unmarked. incoming contains direct incoming target identities, not their entire young closure. Return exactly {incoming:[str],marked:[str],unmarked:[str]}, with each list unique and sorted by ordinary case-sensitive Python lexical ordering. unmarked is the selected set minus marked. Empty graph and empty Y are valid; empty Y does not mean full collection. The result concerns marking and eligibility in this model, not actual memory release, timing, finalization, or a runtime implementation. Returned containers and strings must be exact native dict/list/str values; the optional young input also permits None as specified. Do not mutate any inputs, including by a later call. Calls must be independent and return fresh mutable output containers rather than cached shared results. No outside-domain validation is required. Use only the standard library, with no network or actual garbage-collector invocation.

Implement rc_ownership(events), a serial model of Rust 1.90 Rc/Weak ownership contributions. Every allocation holds a modeled value with one nontrivial, nonpanicking, nonresurrecting destructor; destruction is atomic, with no destructor-induced ledger mutations. There is no count overflow, concurrency, ownership cycle, allocation failure, or allocation-ID reuse. events has at most 100 exact-schema records, with at most 4 allocation IDs, 32 destination handle names, and 16 raw-token names. IDs are case-sensitive ASCII strings matching [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,16}; allocation, handle and token namespaces are separate. Every destination name is fresh and never reused, including the proposed destination of a failed upgrade. Start with empty allocation history, handles and raw tokens. Events: {op:'new',allocation:A,strong:H} creates positive-size backing, a live inner value, one strong handle/count and zero explicit weak count; {op:'clone',source:H,handle:N} clones an existing strong OR weak handle with the same kind (empty Weak clones allocate nothing); {op:'downgrade',strong:H,weak:N} adds explicit weak ownership without changing strong count; {op:'empty_weak',weak:N} models Weak::new with allocation=None; {op:'upgrade',weak:H,strong:N} succeeds and creates a new strong handle/count iff the referenced allocation's maintained strong count is positive, otherwise creates no handle; {op:'drop',handle:H} consumes a handle and decrements its corresponding count; {op:'forget',handle:H} removes accessibility but PRESERVES its count as a forgotten ownership contribution; {op:'into_raw',handle:H,token:T} transfers that one contribution to an opaque raw ownership token without decrementing; {op:'from_raw',token:T,handle:N} consumes a valid token exactly once and restores a handle without changing counts. Tokens represent ownership, not arbitrary copied pointer bits. Empty Weak conversion/restoration carries allocation=None and no allocation or count. All referenced handles/tokens exist with the required kind, and all structural/lifecycle preconditions hold; no invalid-input validation is required. When an ordinary drop removes the final strong contribution, destroy the inner value exactly once in that event and set value_alive=False. Keep backing while any explicit weak contribution remains, including forgotten or raw contributions; otherwise release it. Final weak drop releases backing only when strong==0. Forgetting does not perform either drop. Counts are the logical maintained ownership contributions, not a particular public Weak introspection method. Return a native list of independent snapshots AFTER every event, or [] for no events. Exact keys: {op,upgrade_succeeded,allocations,handles,raw}. upgrade_succeeded is bool only for upgrade and None otherwise. Allocation records persist as history with exactly {strong:int,weak:int,forgotten_strong:int,forgotten_weak:int,value_alive:bool,backing_alive:bool,destructions:int}. Handle and raw-token records are exactly {kind:'strong'|'weak',allocation:A_or_None}; only empty weak records use None. Counts equal accessible-handle plus raw-token plus forgotten contributions. All containers and scalar types are exact built-in dict/list/str/int/bool/None values. Do not mutate inputs, previous snapshots or earlier call results; every snapshot and call is independent. Use only the standard library, without actual Rust execution, raw memory access, threads or network.

Implement arena_lifetimes(capacity, cleanup_on_reset, events), an unchecked symbolic C++-like arena model, not a safe Rust borrowing API or a real memory-access implementation. capacity is a native int from 0 to 64, excluding bool; cleanup_on_reset is a native bool. events has at most 80 exact-schema records, at most 16 fresh allocation IDs (failed attempts also reserve their names against reuse), and at most 16 fresh reference IDs. IDs are case-sensitive ASCII strings matching [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,16}; allocation and reference namespaces are separate. The backing region [0,capacity) remains allocated; cursor starts at 0. Objects use unit alignment with no metadata bytes, size 1–32, and nested_bytes 0–64, all native ints excluding bool. Each successful new object is initialized and has a finite nonthrowing destructor; positive nested_bytes represents one separately allocated buffer. All objects are mutually non-nested and new overlapping objects are nontransparent replacements. Events: {op:'alloc',id,size,nested_bytes} reports no-space with no state mutation if size>capacity-cursor; otherwise construct a fresh complete object at [cursor,cursor+size) and advance cursor. Any LIVE older object whose interval overlaps that new incompatible reuse becomes reused without running a destructor, and its owned nested buffer becomes leaked. Objects not overlapped remain live. {op:'alias',ref:R,object:O} requires live O and creates a nonowning identity reference; {op:'read',ref:R} only classifies that reference, reporting valid while O is live and expired after destruction/reuse, without a real dereference; {op:'drop_ref',ref:R} removes that nonowner without object cleanup; {op:'destroy',object:O} requires live O, invokes its destructor exactly once, changes its state to destroyed and its owned buffer to released, leaving cursor unchanged; {op:'reset'} in raw mode only sets cursor=0, preserving object lifetimes until later destruction or incompatible reuse. With cleanup_on_reset=True, reset first destroys all still-live registered objects in REVERSE successful allocation order, then rewinds. Destroyed/reused records remain as history and are never destroyed again. Equal addresses do not revive old references. There is no implicit end-of-trace cleanup. Return a native list of independent snapshots AFTER every event, or [] for no events. Each snapshot has exactly {op,status,cursor,objects,refs,destructor_log,live_nested_bytes,leaked_nested_bytes}. Statuses are alloc: allocated/no-space; alias: aliased; read: valid/expired; drop_ref: released-reference; destroy: destroyed; reset: reset. Each object record has exactly {start:int,size:int,state:'live'|'destroyed'|'reused',nested_bytes:int,nested_state:'none'|'owned'|'released'|'leaked'}. Zero nested_bytes always uses none; a positive buffer starts owned. live_nested_bytes sums both owned AND leaked buffer amounts that remain allocated; leaked_nested_bytes sums only leaked amounts. refs maps reference IDs to object IDs. destructor_log records invocation order. All containers and scalars are exact built-in dict/list/str/int/bool values of the stated shapes; dict key order is irrelevant. Inputs satisfy all schemas/reference/liveness preconditions, while no-space is an in-domain outcome. Do not mutate inputs, previous snapshots or earlier call results; calls and snapshots are independent. No outside-domain validation is required. Use only the standard library to manipulate model data. Do not invoke a real arena, raw-memory allocation/access API, or the modeled objects' actual destructors. No network; ordinary Python computation and allocation are allowed.

Implement marking_trace(graph, roots, events, barrier=True), a pure serialized interleaving analyzer of the declared fixed-root, no-allocation tricolor marking model. graph is an exact built-in dict containing 0–12 object IDs, each mapped to a fixed-length exact list of 0–8 fields, at most 64 fields total. Each field is None or an existing object ID. IDs are case-sensitive ASCII matching [A-Za-z0-9_]{1,12}. roots is an exact list of 0–24 existing IDs, with duplicates permitted. events is an exact list of at most 64 exact-schema event dicts, and barrier is an exact bool with default True. All objects begin white; discover roots in first-occurrence input order, making each gray and appending it once to a FIFO work queue. Roots remain fixed, no modeled object is allocated, and fields change only through supplied store events. Event {op:'scan'} is one atomic whole-object scan: if gray is nonempty, remove its head, examine all its current fields left-to-right, discover each white nonnull target by making it gray and enqueuing it once, then make the scanned source black. If gray is empty, scan does nothing. Event {op:'store',object:ID,index:int,target:ID_or_None} has a valid object and an index satisfying 0<=index<len(graph[object]); index is a native int, never bool. Before assigning that field, if barrier is True, the source is black, and the new target is nonnull and white, shade/enqueue the target. A gray or white source does not trigger this insertion barrier, and a gray or black target is never queued again. Then assign only the indicated field. Event {op:'finish'} is blocked with no state change while gray is nonempty. Otherwise it atomically finishes the cycle and freezes updates. A successful finish must be the last event; an unsuccessful finish can be followed by more work, and a trace need not finish. Return an exact native list containing an INITIAL snapshot followed by one snapshot after EACH event. Each snapshot has exactly {gray:[IDs_in_queue_order],black:[sorted_IDs],white:[sorted_IDs],finished:bool,missed:[sorted_IDs]}. The three color lists are disjoint, have no duplicates, and cover every object. Before successful finish, missed is empty. At successful finish, recompute current root reachability from the final stored graph and report exactly its still-WHITE objects in missed. This is a diagnostic only: it does not mark or repair those objects, so barrier=False can report an unsound completion. Objects discovered earlier can remain black after their last reachable path is deleted; do not reset marks from final reachability. Sorted lists use ordinary case-sensitive Python lexical ordering. Snapshot containers/scalars must be exact native dict/list/str/bool values; input field targets additionally permit None and store indices are the native integers specified above. Every snapshot and every call must have independent mutable output containers; do not mutate any input, including during a later call, or retain cross-call result state. All stated event preconditions hold, so no outside-domain validation is required. Use only the standard library, with no network, real concurrent threads, raw memory access, or runtime garbage-collector invocation. Ordinary Python computation and allocation are allowed. This bounded analyzer does not claim to implement an arbitrary collector's root, allocation, asynchronous barrier, termination, or reclamation protocol.
